desc_en: In the Yoshimi district of northern Ube, surrounded by farmland and wooded hills, lies the quiet hot spring area of Jisei-ji Onsen. Just a short way from the center of Ube, a city known for its industry, a peaceful countryside opens up. In a simple, unspoiled atmosphere, take your time soaking in waters long loved by locals and let the fatigue of travel melt away.
quiz_en: Ube City is home to Jisei-ji Onsen. What spots or local specialties would you recommend visiting after a relaxing soak here?

desc_en: Yuda Onsen, which springs up in the heart of Yamaguchi City, is known for its founding legend of a wounded white fox that healed itself in the waters. White fox motifs and free footbaths appear all over town, and the hot spring district, lined with ryokan (traditional inns) and hotels, stays lively into the night. It is also the birthplace of the poet Nakahara Chuya, whose literary world you can explore at his memorial museum.
quiz_en: According to the founding legend of Yuda Onsen, which animal is said to have healed its wounds by bathing in the hot spring?

desc_en: Chomonkyo is a gorge about 12 km long carved by the Abu River and designated a national Place of Scenic Beauty. Sheer rock walls, deep pools and clear water continue along its length, and a walking trail lets you enjoy its ever-changing valley scenery. In autumn, colorful leaves paint the river surface, making it one of the prefecture's finest foliage spots. It is also loved as the setting of Nakahara Chuya's poem 'Winter Chomonkyo'.
quiz_en: Poet Nakahara Chuya wrote a poem titled after a particular season at Chomonkyo Gorge. Which season appears in the title of that poem?

desc_en: Standing in the Tokusa area of Ato in Yamaguchi City, Tokusa Hachimangu is a shrine famous for the weeping cherry trees lining its approach. In spring, the long avenue of blossoms turns a soft pink, drawing many cherry blossom viewers. Tokusa lies in a basin among the mountains and is also known as a fruit-growing area with spreading apple orchards, offering simple rural scenery in every season.
quiz_en: After viewing the weeping cherry trees at Tokusa Hachimangu Shrine, which fruit would you want to taste in the Ato area?

name_en: Ryuzo-ji Temple and Ryoun-ji Temple Ruins
desc_en: Set in the mountains of Yoshiki in Yamaguchi City, Ryuzo-ji is an old temple known for the giant ginkgo tree in its grounds and a nearby waterfall. In autumn, the huge tree turns a brilliant gold, creating a stunning sight. Nearby are the ruins of Ryoun-ji, linked to the Ouchi clan, where sturdy stone walls hint at the temple's former scale. It makes for a walk tracing the legacy of the Ouchi culture that once ruled medieval Yamaguchi.
quiz_en: In the grounds of Ryuzo-ji Temple, a large tree turns golden every autumn. What kind of tree is it?

desc_en: Located in the Yunoki area of Tokuji in Yamaguchi City, in the mountains along the Saba River, Yunoki Jisho Onsen is a modest healing spa long cherished by locals. It is surrounded by lush green mountains whose rural scenery shifts with the seasons. Tokuji also has a history of washi (Japanese paper) making, so after your soak, take your time gazing at the peaceful landscape of mountain village life.
quiz_en: Yunoki Jisho Onsen is in the Tokuji area of Yamaguchi City. Which countryside sights would you like to visit after a soak here?

desc_en: Aio Onsen is a hot spring in the Aio district of southern Yamaguchi City. Aio is a town facing Yamaguchi Bay on the Seto Inland Sea, with an open landscape of reclaimed land and seaside parks. The nearby Kirara-hama facilities offer wide lawns and coastal views, so combining a seaside stroll with a relaxing break at the hot spring is highly recommended.
quiz_en: After unwinding at Aio Onsen, what would you like to do along the seashore of Aio?

desc_en: The Chomonkyo Momiji (Autumn Leaves) Festival is held in autumn, when the famous foliage spot of Chomonkyo is at its most colorful. Red and yellow trees decorate the sheer rock walls along the clear Abu River, delighting those walking through the gorge. Around the venue, stalls serving local flavors add to the bustle, letting you experience the season when this quiet mountain gorge is at its liveliest.
quiz_en: After enjoying the autumn leaves at the Chomonkyo Momiji Festival, what other scenery of the gorge would you like to see?

name_en: Suzenji, Omura Shrine and Nagasawa Pond
desc_en: Suzenji in Yamaguchi City takes its name from the ancient minting of coins in Suo Province, and the ruins of the mint remain. The area is also known as the birthplace of Omura Masujiro, a military scholar of the late Edo and Meiji periods, and Omura Shrine is dedicated to him. Nearby Nagasawa Pond is a broad irrigation reservoir, and together with the peaceful farmland it makes for a pleasant historical walk.
quiz_en: Who is the military scholar of the late Edo and Meiji periods, born in Suzenji, who is enshrined at Omura Shrine?

desc_en: Shoin Shrine in Hagi enshrines Yoshida Shoin, a thinker of the late Edo period. In its grounds stands Shokasonjuku, the private school where Shoin taught many young people, preserved as it was. Having produced figures such as Takasugi Shinsaku and Ito Hirobumi, it is a component of the World Heritage Site 'Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution.' Many visitors come to pray for success in exams, as Shoin is revered as a deity of learning.
quiz_en: What is the name of the private school, preserved in the grounds of Shoin Shrine, where Yoshida Shoin taught young people?

desc_en: The Hagi Castle Ruins mark the site of the castle Mori Terumoto built at the foot of Mount Shizuki after the Battle of Sekigahara, now maintained as Shizuki Park. Although the keep was dismantled in the Meiji era, the stone walls reflected in the moat and the keep's base remain, recalling its former grandeur. In spring, cherry blossoms frame the walls, and it is a popular starting point for exploring the castle town of Hagi.
quiz_en: Which warlord built Hagi Castle after the Battle of Sekigahara and laid the foundations of the Choshu domain?

desc_en: Hofu Tenmangu enshrines Sugawara no Michizane and is said to be Japan's first Tenmangu shrine, founded shortly after his death. From the hilltop shrine buildings you can look out over the streets of Hofu, and in plum blossom season the grounds fill with floral fragrance. The autumn Goshinko Festival, in which men in white robes carry a mikoshi (portable shrine), is known as the Hadaka-bo Matsuri and draws large crowds.
quiz_en: The Goshinko Festival at Hofu Tenmangu Shrine has a popular nickname inspired by the men in white robes. What is it called?

desc_en: Kasado Island floats in the Seto Inland Sea south of Kudamatsu and is linked to the mainland by the Kasado Ohashi Bridge. The island has beaches and walking trails overlooking the calm sea, and from its observation points you can enjoy views of many scattered islands. There are also lodgings with hot springs, where you can spend relaxed island time savoring fresh seafood such as the famous local flounder.
quiz_en: Which farmed fish, raised on Kasado Island in Kudamatsu City, is well known as the island's local specialty?

desc_en: Hanaoka Hachimangu in the Suetake area of Kudamatsu has long been revered by local people. The Hanaoka district, on the old San'yo-do highway, has a history as a thriving post town, and the shrine's trees and stone steps create a calm atmosphere. At the autumn festival the whole community comes together in celebration, letting you sense a faith deeply rooted in daily life in Kudamatsu.
quiz_en: After visiting Hanaoka Hachimangu Shrine, what local dish would you like to try in Kudamatsu City?

desc_en: Kudamatsu Shrine is linked to the legend of a star falling onto a pine tree, said to be the origin of the name Kudamatsu. It is closely tied to Myoken worship, which deifies the stars, and shrines conveying this history are scattered across the city. The shrine buildings in the hills of the Kawachi area are surrounded by greenery, inviting you to imagine the night sky and immerse yourself in ancient lore.
quiz_en: According to the legend said to be the origin of the name Kudamatsu, what is it that fell from the sky onto a pine tree?

desc_en: Spanning the Nishiki River in Iwakuni, Kintai Bridge is one of Japan's most celebrated bridges, made of a series of wooden arches. It was built in the Edo period by the Kikkawa clan, lords of the Iwakuni domain, and its intricate woodworking techniques are still passed down each time it is rebuilt. Iwakuni Castle rises on the mountain behind, and the scenery is beautiful in every season, from spring cherry blossoms to summer cormorant fishing.
quiz_en: How many wooden arches are linked together to form Kintai Bridge over the Nishiki River in Iwakuni City?

desc_en: Mount Zenitsubo in the Yu area of Iwakuni is a mountain with sweeping views over the Seto Inland Sea. From near the summit you can see Suo-Oshima and the islands of the Aki Sea, and on clear days even distant mountain ranges. The trail has the feel of a gentle countryside hike, and in the town of Yu at the foot of the mountain, a peaceful way of life unfolds where sea and mountains are close at hand.
quiz_en: If you gazed out over the Seto Inland Sea from the top of Mount Zenitsubo, what kinds of islands did you see?

desc_en: Sozukyo Onsen is a hot spring in the mountains of Nishiki in Iwakuni City. Nishiki lies along the upper reaches of the Nishiki River, an area rich in nature with deep forests and clear streams. The nearby Sozukyo Gorge, shaped by rocks and mountain streams, is pleasant to explore in the seasons of fresh greenery and autumn leaves. Warming up in the hot spring after a gorge walk is a perfect way to enjoy the mountain village.
quiz_en: Sozukyo Onsen is located in Nishiki. Which seasonal scenery would you like to enjoy together with a walk through the gorge?

desc_en: Yu Onsen is a day-trip hot spring facility in the Yu area of Iwakuni City. Yu is a calm town facing the Seto Inland Sea, where coastal views and the mountains behind feel close at hand. Loved as a gathering place by local people, its easygoing atmosphere makes it simple to drop by. During a seaside drive or stroll, you can stop for a relaxing soak and catch your breath.
quiz_en: Yu Onsen is in the town of Yu. What delicious local food would you like to eat when you stop by?

desc_en: Murozumi Park in Hikari is a nature park centered on Mount Gabi, which juts into the Seto Inland Sea. Its coastline of white sand beaches and green pine groves is beautiful and busy with swimmers and walkers. From the peninsula's trails you can take in the calm Suo Sea and its islands, and the town of Murozumi at the foot of the mountain still retains traces of an old port town.
quiz_en: What is the name of the mountain jutting into the Seto Inland Sea that forms the heart of Murozumi Park?

desc_en: Mount Iwaki in Hikari is known for its kogoishi, stone remains believed to be the site of an ancient mountain fortress, and is designated a National Historic Site. Cut stones line up as if circling the mountainside, conveying the large scale of the site. At the summit stands Iwaki Shrine, and from its viewpoints you can look out over the Suo plains and the Seto Inland Sea. The mountain offers both history and great views.
quiz_en: Mount Iwaki has lines of cut stones thought to be part of an ancient mountain fortress. What are these stone remains called?

desc_en: Nagato Yumoto Onsen, with ryokan (traditional inns) lining the Otozure River through the mountains of Nagato, is one of Yamaguchi Prefecture's most historic hot spring resorts. In recent years the riverside has been redeveloped, and its riverside decks and strolling paths have become popular. Enjoy the waters at public baths such as Otoyu, then wander along the lantern-lit riverbank at night for a charming hot spring town experience.
quiz_en: What is the name of the river that flows through the heart of Nagato Yumoto Onsen and is enjoyed from riverside decks?

desc_en: Tawarayama Onsen in Nagato is a mountain hot spring town that has long flourished as a place for therapeutic stays. Most of its inns have no baths of their own, and guests follow the old custom of visiting public baths such as Machi-no-yu and Hakuen-no-yu. A founding legend about a wounded white monkey healed by the waters also survives, and the nostalgic atmosphere of inns along narrow lanes is part of its charm.
quiz_en: According to the founding legend of Tawarayama Onsen, which animal is said to have healed its wounds by soaking in the waters?

desc_en: Yumen Onsen is a small hot spring area in the mountains of Misumi in Nagato City. Misumi is an area of Nagato, on the Sea of Japan side, where riverside farmland and wooded hills spread out gently, so you can enjoy bathing in quiet surroundings. Nearby facilities convey the region's past culture, letting you spend unhurried time in the mountain village alongside the hot spring.
quiz_en: Yumen Onsen is in the Misumi area of Nagato City. Which scenic spot on the Sea of Japan would you visit after your soak?

desc_en: Yuyawan Onsen faces the calm waters of Yuya Bay in the Yuya district of Nagato. The bay opens onto the Sea of Japan yet its waves are gentle, and at dusk the setting sun dyes it orange. Terraced rice fields and peaceful fishing villages surround the area, so you can savor fresh seafood while enjoying the open feeling unique to a seaside hot spring.
quiz_en: Which Sea of Japan seafood would you like to taste while watching the sunset at Yuyawan Onsen?

desc_en: Kibato Onsen is a hot spring near the Sea of Japan in the Heki area of Nagato. Sea and farmland lie close together here, and in summer there is a beach for swimming. Heki is also known for its terraced rice fields, and its peaceful views stretching toward the sea are a highlight. After playing by the sea, wash off in the hot spring and relax while gazing at the evening scenery over the Sea of Japan.
quiz_en: Kibato Onsen is in the Heki area of Nagato City. What scenery there would you most like other travelers to see?

desc_en: Akiyoshido is a limestone cave spreading beneath Akiyoshidai, one of Japan's largest karst plateaus, and is a Special Natural Monument. In the cool interior, formations shaped over long ages appear one after another, such as the Hyakumaizara, terraces of rimstone pools resembling rice paddies and a giant stone pillar called the Golden Pillar. Above ground, you can also enjoy grasslands dotted with limestone rocks typical of karst landscapes.
quiz_en: Akiyoshido Cave has a famous spot where dish-shaped limestone pools line up like terraced rice fields. What is it called?

desc_en: Toron Onsen is a hot spring in the Mito area of Mine City. Mito lies east of Akiyoshidai, a peaceful mountain basin of fields also known for produce such as burdock root. It is easy to visit along with sightseeing on Akiyoshidai and its limestone caves, and you can soothe your tired body after walking the karst plateau.
quiz_en: After walking Akiyoshidai, you take a break at Toron Onsen. Which local specialty would you like to try in Mine City?

desc_en: Suijin Park is located in the Ofuku area of Mine City. Ofuku, in the north of the city, is a quiet area surrounded by mountains and blessed with clear water and greenery. As its name honoring the water deity suggests, the park lets you stroll or rest in a cool waterside atmosphere. Take your time enjoying this relaxing spot, long loved by locals, together with the surrounding countryside scenery.
quiz_en: If you wanted to relax by the water at Suijin Park in the Ofuku area of Mine City, which season would you choose to visit?

desc_en: Taisho Cave is a limestone cave spreading beneath the eastern side of Akiyoshidai. Its interior has a three-dimensional structure that rises and falls, so you climb up and down stairs while observing stalactites, stalagmites and other formations up close. Compared with Akiyoshido, it retains a more rustic feel, and the sense of exploration is part of its appeal. Above ground, karst grasslands spread out around it.
quiz_en: In a limestone cave like Taisho Cave, what do we call the rock formations that hang down from the ceiling and grow over time?

desc_en: Yuno Onsen is a traditional hot spring town in the mountains of Shunan. Ryokan (traditional inns) are scattered along the Yoichi River, letting you spend time in a calm, quiet setting that feels like a classic healing spa. The area is surrounded by rich countryside, and the seasonal scenery, from fresh spring greenery to autumn leaves, is part of the pleasure. Close to central Shunan, it is an easy hot spring to visit.
quiz_en: After relaxing at Yuno Onsen, which spots would you recommend stopping by in Shunan City?

desc_en: Mitsuo Onsen is a hot spring in the former Kumage Town area of Shunan. Peaceful farmland and rolling hills surround it, and it has long been loved by local people. While Shunan is known as an industrial city on the Seto Inland Sea, a little inland you will find calm rural scenery. Soak in the waters and savor the tranquility of the countryside.
quiz_en: After soaking at Mitsuo Onsen, what would you like to do amid the surrounding countryside scenery?

desc_en: Ishifune Onsen is a hot spring in the mountains of Kano in Shunan City. Kano sits in the highlands of the eastern prefecture, an area that stays cool even in summer and is blessed with clear streams and forests. The riverside greenery and clear flowing water are beautiful, and soaking in the hot spring amid nature lets you spend quiet time away from everyday life.
quiz_en: Ishifune Onsen is in the Kano area of Shunan City. Which season would be best for spending time in this cool highland village?

desc_en: Kawasaki Kannon is a hall in the Kawasaki area of Shunan dedicated to Kannon, the Buddhist deity of mercy, and has long drawn the devotion of local people. Though close to residential areas, its grounds are wrapped in a calm atmosphere. Shunan is a port and industrial city facing the Seto Inland Sea, yet places of prayer like this remain part of everyday life. Pause quietly to pray during your stroll.
quiz_en: After visiting Kawasaki Kannon, what scenery in Shunan City would you most like to see?

desc_en: Takase Gorge and Lake Takase in Shunan form a scenic area of deep mountain valleys and a dam lake. In the gorge, clear water threads between rocks under green trees for a refreshing view, while the lake's still surface mirrors the surrounding mountains. It is especially beautiful in the seasons of fresh greenery and autumn leaves, and you can feel the changing seasons on a drive or walk.
quiz_en: If you visited Takase Gorge and Lake Takase, would you recommend the season of fresh greenery or the season of autumn leaves, and why?

desc_en: Mount Bodaiji is a low hill in Sanyo-Onoda City. From near the summit you can look out over the city and the Suo Sea, and it is a popular easy hiking course for local people. Sanyo-Onoda faces the Seto Inland Sea and developed through industries such as cement and ceramics. After working up a sweat on the trail, take the chance to explore the city's history too.
quiz_en: Looking out over Sanyo-Onoda from the summit of Mount Bodaiji, what kind of scenery did you see?

desc_en: Ryuzaki Onsen is a hot spring in the Agenosho area on the south coast of Suo-Oshima. Suo-Oshima is an island in the Seto Inland Sea known for growing mandarin oranges thanks to its warm climate. From the hot spring you can take in views of the calm sea and islands, giving a seaside resort feel. Enjoy it along with island flavors such as sweets made with mandarins.
quiz_en: After bathing at Ryuzaki Onsen on Suo-Oshima, which island specialty fruit would you like to taste?

desc_en: The Seta Hachimangu Autumn Festival is held in Waki, a town at the eastern tip of Yamaguchi Prefecture on the border with Hiroshima Prefecture. Though small, Waki is also an industrial town with large factories along its coast. On festival day, local people gather at the shrine to pray for the harvest and the town's peace. It is an event where you can feel the energy of a community carrying on its traditions.
quiz_en: Thinking of local autumn festivals like the Seta Hachimangu Autumn Festival, what kinds of events are held in your own town?

desc_en: Hannya-ji in the Usagi area of Hirao is a temple with a long history, carefully preserved by local people. Hirao sits at the base of the Murotsu Peninsula, a calm town facing the Seto Inland Sea. The grounds are wrapped in a peaceful atmosphere, and you can worship quietly while admiring seasonal flowers and trees. It is an ideal starting point for a walk exploring the town's history.
quiz_en: After visiting Hannya-ji Temple, which views of the Seto Inland Sea would you like to see in Hirao Town?

desc_en: Sagou Island is a small island off the coast of Hirao. You reach it by regular ferry and are greeted by a quiet village with few people and calm views of the Seto Inland Sea. Walking around the island, time flows simply, wrapped in the sound of waves and the scent of the sea. Unlike busy tourist spots, it lets you savor the relaxed atmosphere unique to the small islands of the Seto Inland Sea.
quiz_en: Sagou Island is a small island in the Seto Inland Sea. If you spent a relaxing day there, what would you like to do?

desc_en: Jinkazan Kofun Park is built around a kofun (ancient burial mound) on a hill in the Saka area of Hirao. From the mound you can look out over calm Seto Inland Sea views such as Hirao Bay, and sense why ancient people chose this place to rest. Burial mounds are scattered around Hirao, letting you reflect on ancient history amid the scenery of sea and hills.
quiz_en: Looking out over the Seto Inland Sea from the hill at Jinkazan Kofun Park, what kind of scenery did you see?

desc_en: Tokushima Prefecture is home to the first temple of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage and is called the 'dojo of awakening,' where many henro (pilgrims) begin their journey. Settai, in which people along the route offer pilgrims tea or sweets to encourage them, is a culture unique to Shikoku that has been handed down for generations. You can witness warm exchanges between pilgrims in white robes and sedge hats and local people.
quiz_en: On the Shikoku pilgrimage, the walking staff carried by henro pilgrims is said to be proof that they walk together with whom?

desc_en: Awa Odori is one of Japan's most famous Bon dances, held mainly in Tokushima City during the Obon season. Dance groups called ren parade through the streets to the lively music of shamisen, bells and drums. The contrast between the bold men's dance and the graceful women's dance is a highlight, and with the well-known chant 'the dancers are fools and the watchers are fools', the audience is swept up in the excitement too.
quiz_en: A famous Awa Odori chant says the dancers are fools and the watchers are fools too. How does the well-known saying continue?

desc_en: Kuramoto Park is a park in urban Tokushima equipped with sports facilities such as a baseball stadium, loved by residents as a place for exercise and relaxation. It has many cherry trees, and in spring it bustles with people enjoying the blossoms. Tokushima is a city of water and greenery embraced by Mount Bizan and the Yoshino River, and this is a familiar park to drop by during a walk or jog.
quiz_en: After working up a sweat at Kuramoto Park, what local food would you like to eat in Tokushima City?

desc_en: Awa Jurobe Yashiki is a museum built on the former residence of Bando Jurobe, said to be the model for the ningyo joruri (puppet theater) play 'Keisei Awa no Naruto'. It displays puppets and materials of the Awa puppet theater rooted in Tokushima, and you can also watch live performances. It is a place to experience up close the puppet theater culture of Tokushima, where many rural stages still survive.
quiz_en: What is the title of the puppet theater play featuring Jurobe that is performed at Awa Jurobe Yashiki?

desc_en: Bunka no Mori (Forest of Culture) Park is set on the hills of Hachiman in Tokushima City and brings together many cultural facilities. The prefectural museum, modern art museum, library and archives are gathered here, so you can learn about Tokushima's nature, history and art all at once. The spacious, green grounds are perfect for strolling, and you can spend a whole day enjoying the scenery of each season.
quiz_en: If you spent a whole day at Bunka no Mori Park, would you visit the museum or the art museum first, and why?

desc_en: The Naruto Whirlpools are giant eddies formed in the Naruto Strait by the ebb and flow of the tides, and during spring tides they are said to reach up to 20 m across, among the largest in the world. You can enjoy them from various angles, feeling their power up close from a sightseeing boat or looking straight down on them from the Uzu-no-Michi walkway of the Onaruto Bridge.
quiz_en: What is the name of the bridge that passes directly over the Naruto Whirlpools and connects Awaji Island with Shikoku?

desc_en: Naruto Uchinoumi Park lies on the shore of Uchinoumi, an inner sea enclosed by Shimada Island and Oge Island in Naruto. With calm waters and green hills spreading across its grounds, you can enjoy walks, picnics and sports. While Naruto is known for its whirlpools, Uchinoumi is a quiet sea where you can also see fishing-village scenery with floating aquaculture rafts.
quiz_en: After spending time at Naruto Uchinoumi Park, what seafood would you like to taste in Naruto?

desc_en: The Naruto Uzu (Whirlpool) Festival is a summer festival held in Naruto, the town of whirlpools. Dances, parades and other events take place in the streets, with residents and visitors celebrating together. Naruto's local specialties include Naruto Kintoki sweet potatoes, wakame seaweed and sea bream, so along with the bustle of a summer night, you can fully enjoy the energy of this seaside town.
quiz_en: Amid the bustle of the Naruto Uzu Festival, which famous Naruto local food would you like to try?

desc_en: Ryozen-ji in the Oasa area of Naruto is the first temple of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. Many henro (pilgrims) gather their white robes, sedge hats, walking staffs and other pilgrimage gear here and set out after praying for a safe journey. Countless lanterns hanging from the main hall's ceiling create a magical atmosphere, and carp swim in the pond in the grounds. It is where pilgrimage culture begins.
quiz_en: Many pilgrims begin their journey at Ryozen-ji Temple. What number does it hold among the temples of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage?

desc_en: Chorakuen Onsen is a hot spring in the Higashiyama area of Nakata in Komatsushima City. Komatsushima is a port town facing the Kii Channel that once thrived as the gateway for sea routes linking Tokushima with the Kansai region. Set a little way into the hills from the town center, the hot spring lets you soak in quiet surroundings. After strolling the port town and enjoying its seafood, relax and soothe away your fatigue.
quiz_en: After soaking at Chorakuen Onsen, what local food would you like to try in the port town of Komatsushima?

desc_en: Tatsue-ji in the Tatsue area of Komatsushima is Temple No. 19 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. It is known as one of Awa's 'checkpoint temples,' where, according to tradition, those with evil deeds in their hearts cannot proceed further, making it a temple that tests the pilgrim's state of mind. Passing through the vermilion gate, you enter spacious grounds where many pilgrims pray with a sense of solemnity.
quiz_en: Pilgrimage temples like Tatsue-ji, beyond which those with evil deeds are said to be unable to proceed, are known by what special name?

desc_en: Omatsu Daigongen in the Kamo area of Anan is a shrine known for worshipping a cat as a deity. It is linked to an Edo-period legend of a ghost cat's revenge, and its grounds are filled with countless beckoning cat figurines and cat statues offered by worshippers. It is said to bring luck in contests and exams, drawing students and cat lovers from all over Japan.
quiz_en: What kind of animal figurines have been offered in great numbers by worshippers in the grounds of Omatsu Daigongen?

desc_en: Anan Seibu Park is laid out on the hills of the Nakaono area of Anan City. With a wide lawn, playground equipment and sports facilities, it is a popular place for families to relax. From the high ground you can look out over the streets of Anan and the surrounding mountains. Anan, through which the Naka River flows, is the main city of southern Tokushima and offers the charms of both sea and mountains.
quiz_en: If you spent the day on the big lawn at Anan Seibu Park, what kinds of games or activities would you like to enjoy?

desc_en: The Ikatake Festival is held in Anan, a city with deep ties to bamboo. Blessed with a warm climate, Anan is also known for producing bamboo shoots. The event reflects a wish to protect bamboo groves and make use of bamboo as a local resource, and decorations and lights made of bamboo brighten the venue. It is a chance to feel the richness of a life lived alongside bamboo.
quiz_en: Anan City is known for its bamboo shoots. What games or crafts would you like to try making with bamboo?

desc_en: Byodo-ji in the Arano area of Anan is Temple No. 22 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. It has a legend of a well said to have sprung up when Kobo Daishi trained here, and some people visit seeking its sacred water. From the main hall at the top of the stone steps in its quiet grounds, surrounded by mountain farmland, you can enjoy views of the peaceful village of Arano.
quiz_en: Byodo-ji Temple in Anan City is linked to Kobo Daishi. What number does it hold among the Shikoku 88 pilgrimage temples?

desc_en: Akedani Plum Grove spreads across the mountains of the Nagaike area of Anan. In early spring, white and red plum blossoms cover the slopes, creating a countryside scene wrapped in sweet fragrance. Because plum trees bloom while the cold still lingers, their flowers are cherished as the first sign of approaching spring. Walk the paths and enjoy an early taste of the season.
quiz_en: After enjoying the blossoms at Akedani Plum Grove, what food or drink made with plums would you like to try?

desc_en: Fuigo Onsen is a hot spring in the Yamakawa area of Yoshinogawa City. Yamakawa lies on the south bank of the Yoshino River, a nature-rich area backed by mountains such as Mount Kotsu. Soaking in the quiet mountain setting helps everyday fatigue melt away. Nearby are famous flower spots and hiking courses, so you can combine the hot spring with nature walks.
quiz_en: Fuigo Onsen is in the Yamakawa area of Yoshinogawa City. Which mountain or river views would you like to admire after your soak?

desc_en: The Gokuro Festival is a local festival held in Yoshinogawa City. The city spreads along the great Yoshino River, also called Shikoku Saburo, and is blessed with abundant water and farmland. On festival day, local people gather and the event bustles with stage shows and food stalls. It is a fun occasion to feel the community's energy and the bonds between its people firsthand.
quiz_en: At local festivals like the Gokuro Festival, what food from the stalls can you never resist buying?

desc_en: Funakubo Azalea Park is a famous azalea spot high in the mountains near Mount Kotsu in the Yamakawa area of Yoshinogawa City. The Ontsutsuji azaleas growing here in clusters are designated a National Natural Monument, and the sight of large bushes bursting into vermilion bloom all at once is breathtaking. At peak season the slopes seem to blaze with color, attracting many flower lovers.
quiz_en: Which variety of azalea, designated a National Natural Monument, grows in clusters at Funakubo Azalea Park?

desc_en: Fujii-dera in the Kamojima area of Yoshinogawa City is Temple No. 11 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. True to its name, meaning 'wisteria well temple,' its grounds have a splendid wisteria trellis, and in season purple clusters hang down to greet visitors. From here a steep mountain path leads to Temple No. 12, Shosan-ji, so this is where pilgrims steel themselves before the first difficult stretch known as 'henro korogashi.'
quiz_en: In the grounds of Fujii-dera Temple, which flower blooms in spring with splendid hanging clusters?

desc_en: The Plum Blossom Festival is held in early spring, when the plums bloom, in places such as the Misato district of Yoshinogawa City, known as a plum village. White and red plum blossoms open on the mountain slopes, and the whole village is wrapped in a gentle fragrance. Misato produces plums, and processed products such as umeshu (plum liqueur) are local specialties. Walking through the village among the blossoms, you can feel spring arriving early.
quiz_en: After feeling spring at the Plum Blossom Festival, which plum product would you like to taste in the plum village of Misato?

desc_en: Okumiyagawauchi Nature Park is a nature park in the mountains of the Donari area of Awa City. Located at the foot of the Asan Mountains and surrounded by clear streams and trees, it is a place to enjoy playing in the river and resting in the shade in summer. Donari is also an area dotted with Shikoku pilgrimage temples, and restaurants serving the local specialty tarai udon are nearby.
quiz_en: After playing in the river at Okumiyagawauchi Nature Park, what local specialty would you like to eat in the Donari area?

desc_en: Horin-ji in the Donari area of Awa City is Temple No. 9 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. Its principal image is a reclining Nirvana Buddha, a rare example among the 88 temples. The calm grounds, set among rice fields, are wrapped in the peaceful atmosphere of the Awa countryside. There is also a custom of offering straw sandals, and worshippers visit to pray for healthy legs and back.
quiz_en: The principal image of Horin-ji Temple is a Buddha statue in an unusual pose. In what posture is the Buddha shown?

desc_en: Gosho tarai udon is a local dish long enjoyed along the Miyagawauchi River in the Donari area of Awa City. Boiled udon noodles are placed with their hot water in a large tarai (wooden tub), and everyone gathers around to dip them in a sauce. A distinctive feature is the broth for the dipping sauce, made from local river fish such as jinzoku. Sharing it with a big group at a riverside restaurant makes for a lively meal.
quiz_en: What is the local name of the river fish used to make the broth for the dipping sauce of Gosho tarai udon?

desc_en: Kirihata-ji in the Ichiba area of Awa City is Temple No. 10 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. It stands halfway up a mountain, and visitors climb a long flight of stone steps to reach the main hall. The temple's name is said to come from the legend of a weaving girl who cut cloth and offered it to Kobo Daishi. Its grounds hold a great pagoda designated an Important Cultural Property, and from the heights you can view the plains of the Yoshino River.
quiz_en: Roughly how many stone steps make up the long staircase leading to the main hall of Kirihata-ji, Temple No. 10?

desc_en: Gosho no Sato is a natural hot spring facility in the Donari area of Awa City. It sits in a peaceful area spreading out at the foot of the Asan Mountains, with Shikoku pilgrimage temples scattered nearby. It is cherished as a bath that soothes the weariness of henro (pilgrims) and serves as a relaxing spot for locals. Soak while gazing at the green mountains and enjoy some unhurried time.
quiz_en: Pilgrimage temples are scattered around Gosho no Sato Natural Onsen. Which temples would you like to visit on your own pilgrimage?

desc_en: Dochu Kyuyomura Onsen is a hot spring in the Awa area of Awa City. Nearby is the National Natural Monument Awa no Dochu (earth pillars), a rare landform where layers of gravel and sand have been left standing like pillars after long years of erosion. It is said to be a rare landscape even by world standards, and after viewing its powerful forms from the observation area, resting at the hot spring is recommended.
quiz_en: What is the landform near Dochu Kyuyomura Onsen, shaped by erosion and designated a National Natural Monument?

desc_en: The udatsu townscape in Wakimachi, Mima City, is a street lined with merchant houses that prospered from the indigo trade from the Edo to Meiji periods. The udatsu, walls built at both ends of the roofs, were for fire prevention and also symbolized wealthy merchants. They are said to be the origin of a Japanese expression about failing to get ahead in life, and the beautiful streets of white walls and tiled roofs still remain today.
quiz_en: Merchant houses in Wakimachi have walls called udatsu at both ends of their roofs. What was their original purpose?

desc_en: Standing 1,955 m tall, Mount Tsurugi is a famous Shikoku peak, second in western Japan only to Mount Ishizuchi. A chairlift runs up from Minokoshi, so you can aim for the summit with relative ease. Gentle bamboo-grass meadows spread near the top, and on clear days you can see the mountains of Shikoku. A legend says fleeing Heike warriors left a treasured sword here, and it has long been revered as a sacred mountain.
quiz_en: Mount Tsurugi is the highest peak in Tokushima and second in western Japan only to Mount Ishizuchi. How tall is it in meters?

desc_en: Matsuogawa Onsen lies in a deep mountain valley along the Matsuo River in the Ikeda area of Miyoshi City. It is surrounded by deep greenery, with the soothing sounds of a clear river and birdsong. Miyoshi is located on the upper reaches of the Yoshino River and is known for remote areas such as Oboke, Koboke and Iya. Use this quiet mountain spa as a base for exploring these hidden regions and take a breather.
quiz_en: After resting at Matsuogawa Onsen, which remote scenic spots would you like to visit in Miyoshi City?

desc_en: The Iya Kazurabashi is a suspension bridge woven from plant vines that spans the gorge of the Iya River. Made by weaving together a plant called shirakuchi-kazura, it is rebuilt every three years. You can see the river through the gaps beneath your feet, and the thrill of it swaying with every step is exceptional. Symbolizing Iya, a remote area with legends of fleeing Heike warriors, it is a nationally designated Important Tangible Folk Cultural Property.
quiz_en: What is the name of the plant that is woven together to make the Iya Kazurabashi Vine Bridge?

desc_en: Oboke Gorge was formed as the rapid currents of the Yoshino River carved through rock over long ages. Aboard a sightseeing boat, you can glide across the emerald-green water while viewing patterned crystalline schist cliffs up close. It is especially beautiful during the fresh greenery of spring and the autumn foliage, and many people visit this gateway to the remote areas of Shikoku.
quiz_en: The cliffs seen from the Oboke Gorge sightseeing boat are made mainly of what type of rock?

desc_en: The Okawara Highlands spread across the mountaintops of Sanagochi Village at a high elevation. Large wind turbines line the ridge, and their slowly turning blades create a striking landscape. In early summer, many hydrangeas burst into bloom and color the highlands. From the observation point you can look out over Tokushima City and the Kii Channel, making it a popular drive destination.
quiz_en: What are the large structures lined up along the ridge of the Okawara Highlands that use the power of the wind to make electricity?

desc_en: Tokuon-ji is a temple in the mountains of Sanagochi Village. Sanagochi is the only village in Tokushima Prefecture, a peaceful place where terraced rice fields and rural scenery remain despite its closeness to central Tokushima City. It is also known for produce such as strawberries and sudachi citrus. Pray in the quiet mountain grounds and take your time savoring the atmosphere of a traditional farming village.
quiz_en: Sanagochi is the only village in Tokushima Prefecture. Which local fruit would you like to taste when you visit?

desc_en: The Ishii Wisteria Festival is held in spring when the wisteria reaches full bloom. Ishii has made wisteria its town flower and is known as a wisteria spot, with splendid trellises remaining at temples and elsewhere. The sight of purple flower clusters swaying in the breeze is elegant, and a sweet scent drifts through the air. Spend a calm spring day in this rural town just west of Tokushima City.
quiz_en: At the Ishii Wisteria Festival you can see many hanging wisteria clusters. What color of wisteria do you like best?

desc_en: Amagoi Falls in Kamiyama is a famous waterfall selected as one of Japan's Top 100 Waterfalls. As you climb the mountain path, several small falls appear along the way, and at the far end you are greeted by a male and a female waterfall cascading side by side. The name, meaning 'rain prayer,' is said to come from prayers for rain held here during droughts. It is a pleasant spot with the coolness and sound of water in a green valley.
quiz_en: At the far end of Amagoi Falls, two waterfalls cascade side by side. What are these two falls called?

desc_en: Shosan-ji in Kamiyama is Temple No. 12 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage, set high on a mountain. The route from Fujii-dera involves steep climbs and descents and is known as the first of the difficult sections called 'henro korogashi' (pilgrim tumbler). In the grounds, huge cedar trees tower over you in a solemn atmosphere. It is a temple where you can pray with a real sense of achievement.
quiz_en: Like the steep pilgrim path leading to Shosan-ji Temple, the toughest sections of the Shikoku pilgrimage are known by what name?

desc_en: Kamiyama Forest Park is a forest park in the mountains of the Ano area of Kamiyama. The spacious grounds have walking trails, an observation deck and lawns, where you can enjoy forest bathing and nature watching. Kamiyama is a town blessed with rich forests and clear streams and is also known for producing sudachi citrus. Seasonal flowers, fresh greenery and autumn leaves let you feel the changing seasons in the forest.
quiz_en: After forest bathing at Kamiyama Forest Park, which local citrus fruit of Kamiyama Town would you like to taste?

desc_en: The Myoo-ji Weeping Cherry Festival is held in spring at Myoo-ji Temple in the Shimobun area of Kamiyama, when its weeping cherry trees reach full bloom. In the grounds of this mountain village temple, the sight of branches heavy with blossoms swaying in the wind captivates visitors. Peaceful countryside spreads through the mountains of Kamiyama, and you can enjoy a springtime view where cherry blossoms and village scenery become one.
quiz_en: At the Myoo-ji Weeping Cherry Festival, what snacks or treats would you like to enjoy while viewing the blossoms?

desc_en: Momijigawa Onsen is a hot spring along the Naka River in Naka Town. As its name, meaning 'autumn leaf river,' suggests, the mountains along the river turn red and gold in autumn, and you can admire the beautiful scenery after your bath. Naka is a deeply mountainous area in southern Tokushima, long supported by forestry and the blessings of clear streams. Rest your body and mind in this quiet mountain village while feeling the flow of the river.
quiz_en: After admiring the autumn leaves at Momijigawa Onsen, what mountain delicacies would you like to taste in Naka Town?

name_en: Konose Gorge Rest House Taira no Sato
desc_en: Konose Gorge is a valley on the upper Naka River in the Kito area of Naka Town, known as a famous spot for autumn foliage. Trees in red and yellow color the sheer mountainsides, contrasting beautifully with the deep valley. Rest House Taira no Sato, along the gorge, is a popular rest stop for drivers. Kito is a mountain village also known for producing yuzu citrus.
quiz_en: Konose Gorge is in the Kito area of Naka Town. What fragrant citrus fruit is the area known for producing?

desc_en: Shikibidani Onsen is a hot spring in the mountains of the Yokotani area of Naka Town. As its name, meaning 'valley beautiful in all four seasons,' suggests, you can enjoy lovely valley scenery in every season: fresh greenery in spring, deep green in summer, autumn foliage and winter stillness. The surroundings are rich in nature with clear streams, perfect for river play and walks. Soak at your leisure in the quiet of the mountain village.
quiz_en: Inspired by the name of Shikibidani Onsen, which season's mountain scenery do you love the most, and why?

desc_en: Teba Island is a small island off the coast of Mugi, where a quiet fishing village with no cars remains. Its traditional houses feature a style called 'mise-zukuri,' with fold-up wooden benches, and the village has been selected as a nationally designated Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. Walking the narrow lanes, you are surrounded by relaxed island life and the scent of the sea.
quiz_en: What is the name of the traditional house style seen on Teba Island, featuring fold-up wooden benches at the front?

desc_en: Jozen no Yu Onigaiwaya Onsen is a hot spring in the Tachibana area of Mugi. Mugi is a town in southern Tokushima surrounded by sea and mountains, with rich fishing grounds blessed by the Kuroshio Current. After a seaside walk or island hopping, you can relax in the bath and warm a body chilled by the sea breeze. The easygoing air of the mild south of the prefecture flows here.
quiz_en: Onigaiwaya Onsen is in Mugi Town. Which seafood from southern Tokushima would you like to eat after your soak?

desc_en: Oshima and Tsushima are islands off the coast of Mugi. Thanks to the Kuroshio Current, the surrounding waters are warm, and a rich underwater landscape of coral and colorful fish spreads out below. The waters around Mugi Oshima are known for coral that has grown large over many years, making it a popular diving spot. Many visitors also come to enjoy rock fishing.
quiz_en: If you went diving in the waters around Oshima and Tsushima off Mugi, which sea creatures would you like to see?

desc_en: Utsuma Beach in the Utsuma area of Mugi is a popular surfing spot thanks to the good waves rolling in from the Pacific Ocean. Green mountains rise close behind the sandy beach, creating scenery typical of southern Tokushima, where sea and mountains are near each other. In summer, swimmers also visit. Take a leisurely stroll along the shore while listening to the sound of the waves.
quiz_en: Many surfers gather at Utsuma Beach. What would you like to try out in the ocean there?

desc_en: Fudosan Shokan-ji is a temple in the Nakamura area of Mugi. Mugi is a town in southern Tokushima on the Shikoku pilgrimage route, with a calm setting surrounded by sea and mountains. The temple's mountain grounds are wrapped in a quiet atmosphere and have been carefully protected by local people. Visit during a stroll through the port town and quietly pray for a safe journey.
quiz_en: After visiting Fudosan Shokan-ji Temple, which seaside spots would you like to stop by in Mugi Town?

desc_en: Yakuo-ji in the Hiwasa area of Minami Town is Temple No. 23 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage and the last temple in Awa Province. It is known as a temple for warding off misfortune, and on the stone steps to the main hall you can see worshippers in their unlucky years placing a coin on each step as they climb. From the Yugi Pagoda on the hill, you can see the town of Hiwasa and the Pacific Ocean, a fitting view to conclude the Awa pilgrimage.
quiz_en: Yakuo-ji Temple draws many worshippers for a particular kind of blessing. What is the temple especially known for?

desc_en: The Shishikui Gion Festival is a summer festival held in the Shishikui area of Kaiyo Town. Shishikui is a Pacific coast town near the border with Kochi Prefecture that has long prospered as a port. On festival day, local people parade mikoshi (portable shrines) and festival floats, and the town is filled with excitement. In this town embraced by summer sea and mountains, you can feel the spirit of people who keep their traditions alive.
quiz_en: At summer festivals like the Shishikui Gion Festival, what is your favorite event or highlight to watch?

desc_en: The Osato Hachiman Shrine Grand Festival is an autumn festival held at the Hachiman Shrine in the Osato area of Kaiyo Town. The pine forest surrounding the grounds, called Osato Matsubara, becomes the festival's stage along with the seaside scenery. On festival day, local people parade mikoshi (portable shrines) and floats, praying for a rich harvest and safety at sea. You can experience the energy of a bold festival handed down in this seaside town.
quiz_en: At autumn festivals like the Osato Hachiman Shrine Grand Festival, would you rather help carry a mikoshi or pull a festival float?

desc_en: Kisogawa Onsen is a hot spring in the Shiimoto area of Kamiita. Kamiita spreads along the north bank of the Yoshino River at the foot of the Asan Mountains and was once known for indigo cultivation and wasanbon sugar making. In peaceful surroundings of farmland and mountains, you can enjoy a quiet soak. After your bath, try sweets made with wasanbon and its refined sweetness.
quiz_en: Which refined local sugar, a specialty of Tokushima, would you like to taste in sweets after a soak at Kisogawa Onsen?

desc_en: Taisan-ji in the Jinge area of Kamiita is an old temple in the Asan Mountains and the first temple of the Shikoku Bekkaku 20 Pilgrimage. Every January it hosts the Chikara Mochi event, in which participants compete to see how far they can walk while carrying a giant rice cake, attracting many spectators. The mountain grounds are wrapped in greenery, and the views over the surroundings are another attraction. Feel the calm air of a quiet mountain temple.
quiz_en: What is the name of the yearly event at Taisan-ji Temple in which participants walk while carrying a giant rice cake?

desc_en: Tsurugisan Yuuma Onsen is a hot spring in the Sadamitsu area of Tsurugi Town. Sadamitsu is the gateway to the trails up Mount Tsurugi, and an old townscape with udatsu walls remains as a reminder of its days as a thriving trading town. Stop by after a hike or drive in the Mount Tsurugi area, and let the water slowly loosen your body. Relax in the clean air of the mountain village.
quiz_en: Tsurugisan Yuuma Onsen is in Sadamitsu. What are the fireproof walls seen in the town's old streets called?

desc_en: Todoro Falls is a waterfall in the mountains of the Handa area of Tsurugi Town. Surrounded by deep forest, its water flows down the rock face with a refreshing sound. Handa is known for hand-pulled somen noodles, and the clear mountain water and cold winter winds have supported the making of firm somen. Viewing the falls in summer followed by cold somen is a special treat.
quiz_en: What noodle dish is the Handa area of Tsurugi Town, home to Todoro Falls, famous for producing?

name_en: Island Scenery of the Seto Inland Sea
desc_en: The Seto Inland Sea spreads north of Kagawa Prefecture, offering beautiful views of islands large and small. From viewpoints in Takamatsu such as Yashima and Mount Mine, you can take in superb panoramas of islands overlapping on the calm sea, and at dusk the water glows gold. Traveling between the islands by ferry, you can also encounter the different ways of life and art on each island.
quiz_en: What is the name of the flat-topped mountain in Takamatsu City that offers sweeping views of the islands of the Seto Inland Sea?

desc_en: In the Shikoku pilgrimage, Kagawa Prefecture is called the 'dojo of nirvana,' where pilgrims complete their journey around the 88 temples. Along the routes to the temples, a culture of settai is deeply rooted, in which local people offer pilgrims food and drink. Temples are also scattered around Takamatsu, and warm exchanges between white-robed pilgrims and locals are part of everyday life in Sanuki.
quiz_en: Kagawa Prefecture is where pilgrims complete the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. What kind of 'dojo' is Kagawa called on the pilgrimage?

desc_en: Ritsurin Garden in Takamatsu is a daimyo (feudal lord) garden built against the backdrop of Mount Shiun and designated a Special Place of Scenic Beauty. Shaped by generations of Takamatsu domain lords, it features six ponds and thirteen artificial hills, and the scenery changes with every step. There are many highlights, such as carefully tended pines and the Engetsu Bridge, and you can even view the garden from the ponds aboard a traditional wooden boat.
quiz_en: What is the name of the mountain that rises behind Ritsurin Garden and serves as its borrowed scenery?

desc_en: Sanuki udon is the signature local dish of Kagawa Prefecture. It is known for its firm, chewy texture and smoothness, and the prefecture is home to countless udon shops, many of them self-service places where you warm the noodles yourself and choose your toppings. There are many ways to eat it, such as kake, bukkake and kamatama, and it is not unusual to see people enjoying udon first thing in the morning.
quiz_en: Kagawa Prefecture is famous for Sanuki udon. What nickname does Kagawa use for itself in its tourism promotion?

desc_en: The Great Seto Bridge is the collective name for the bridges connecting Kurashiki in Okayama Prefecture with Sakaide in Kagawa Prefecture, crossing the Seto Inland Sea via several islands. It is a combined road and rail bridge, with cars running on the upper deck and trains on the lower deck, and its grand scale makes it an iconic sight of the Seto Inland Sea. Seen from places such as Seto Ohashi Memorial Park in Sakaide, the bridge looks especially beautiful against the setting sun.
quiz_en: Cars travel on the upper deck of the Great Seto Bridge. What runs along the lower deck of the bridge?

desc_en: Benesse Art Site Naoshima is the collective name for contemporary art activities on Naoshima and other islands of the Seto Inland Sea. At the Chichu Art Museum and Benesse House, both designed by Ando Tadao, you can experience spaces where architecture, nature and art become one. The polka-dot pumpkin by Kusama Yayoi placed by the sea is known as a symbol of the island, and travelers come from all over the world.
quiz_en: Who is the artist behind the famous polka-dot pumpkin sculpture placed by the sea on Naoshima Island?

desc_en: Kotohiragu in Kotohira, affectionately known as 'Konpira-san,' has long been worshipped as the guardian deity of maritime travel. A long flight of stone steps leads to the main shrine halfway up Mount Zozu, and the approach is lined with souvenir shops and udon restaurants. In the Edo period, a pilgrimage to Konpira was a dream for ordinary people, and today many worshippers still climb the steps one by one.
quiz_en: How many stone steps in total lead from the entrance of the approach to the main shrine of Kotohiragu Shrine?

name_en: Kabuki at the Old Konpira Grand Theater (Kanamaru-za)
desc_en: The Old Konpira Grand Theater in Kotohira, commonly called Kanamaru-za, was built in the Edo period and is designated an Important Cultural Property as Japan's oldest surviving playhouse. At the Shikoku Konpira Kabuki Grand Performance held here every spring, you can enjoy a unique sense of presence, with the actors close to the audience amid traditional mechanisms such as a hand-powered revolving stage and a trapdoor lift called suppon.
quiz_en: The Shikoku Konpira Kabuki Grand Performance is held every year at Kanamaru-za. In which season does this event take place?

desc_en: In the Shikoku pilgrimage, Ehime Prefecture is called the 'dojo of enlightenment,' and many pilgrimage temples are gathered in Matsuyama, including Ishite-ji near Dogo Onsen. Along the pilgrim routes, you can see settai, in which local people hand mandarin oranges or tea to henro (pilgrims). This culture of warmly welcoming unknown travelers is a heartfelt hospitality deeply rooted in the lives of the people of Shikoku.
quiz_en: Of the four 'dojo' of the Shikoku pilgrimage, what kind of dojo is Ehime Prefecture called?

desc_en: Mount Takanawa is the main peak of the Takanawa Peninsula, rising in northern Matsuyama. From near the summit you can look out over the Matsuyama Plain and the islands of the Seto Inland Sea, and on clear days a magnificent view spreads out. Forests cover the mountain, and you can enjoy nature by hiking or driving. Just a short trip from central Matsuyama, you can experience rich mountain nature.
quiz_en: Gazing over the Matsuyama Plain and the Seto Inland Sea from the summit of Mount Takanawa, what kind of view did you see?

desc_en: Kashima is a small island off the Hojo area of Matsuyama, reachable in just a few minutes by ferry. Wild deer live on the island, and you can come across them relaxing at their leisure. In summer it bustles as a swimming beach, and from the walking trail circling the island you can enjoy calm views of the Seto Inland Sea. It is loved as a symbol of the Hojo seaside.
quiz_en: Kashima Island off Hojo in Matsuyama City is home to an animal that also gives the island its name. Which animal is it?

desc_en: The Shimanami Kaido is a route linking Imabari in Ehime Prefecture and Onomichi in Hiroshima Prefecture via bridges that connect islands of the Seto Inland Sea. Bridges of different types, such as suspension and cable-stayed bridges, follow one another, and the Kurushima Kaikyo Bridge, the world's first triple suspension bridge, is especially spectacular. With paths for cyclists and pedestrians, it draws people from around the world as a cycling mecca.
quiz_en: What is the name of the world's first triple suspension bridge on the Shimanami Kaido, linking Imabari City and Oshima Island?

desc_en: Imabari Castle is a seaside castle built by Todo Takatora, known as a master castle builder. With wide moats filled with seawater from the Seto Inland Sea, it is counted among Japan's three great water castles. Sea fish swim in the moats, and the water level changes with the tides. The current keep is a reconstruction, and from its upper floors you can view the city of Imabari and the Seto Inland Sea.
quiz_en: Which warlord, famed as a master castle builder, constructed Imabari Castle by the Seto Inland Sea?

desc_en: Yunoura Onsen is a hot spring area on the outskirts of Imabari, dotted with hotels and ryokan (traditional inns). Surrounded by green hills, it is also conveniently located as a base for sightseeing on the Shimanami Kaido. Imabari is known for producing towels, and local dishes such as yakibuta tamago meshi (roast pork and egg rice) are popular. After cycling around the islands, soothe your tired body in the hot spring.
quiz_en: Yunoura Onsen is in Imabari City. What specialty product is Imabari famous for throughout Japan?

desc_en: Nibukawa Onsen is a hot spring area in the mountains of the Tamagawa area of Imabari. Inns line the Nibukawa Gorge, where you can spend quiet time listening to the murmur of the clear stream. Walking the gorge is enjoyable in the seasons of fresh greenery and autumn leaves, and in summer the coolness of the riverside is refreshing. Though close to central Imabari, it has the charm of a hidden village deep in the mountains.
quiz_en: If you were to walk through the gorge at Nibukawa Onsen, would you prefer the season of fresh greenery or autumn leaves?

desc_en: Uwajima Castle is based on a castle built by Todo Takatora, with the keep later rebuilt by the Date family when they became lords of the domain. The keep is one of the twelve original castle keeps surviving from the Edo period, small yet elegant. The castle hill is covered in greenery, and from the keep at the top of the stone steps you can see the town of Uwajima and the Uwa Sea. Uwajima is a castle town rich in seafood such as tai meshi (sea bream rice).
quiz_en: Like the keep of Uwajima Castle, some original castle keeps survive from the Edo period or earlier. How many are there in Japan?

desc_en: The Teramachi district of Uwajima is a calm area where temples are clustered in one part of the castle town. Many temples are linked to the Date family of the Uwajima domain, and walking the lanes lined with tiled roofs and earthen walls, you can feel the quiet charm of a castle town. Seasonal flowers and trees decorate the temple grounds, offering a stroll away from the bustle. Combine it with Uwajima Castle for a historical walk.
quiz_en: After strolling through the Teramachi district, which local dish would you like to taste in Uwajima City?

desc_en: Yoshida Park is a park in the Yoshida area of Uwajima City. Yoshida has a history as the jinya (administrative) town of the Yoshida domain, a branch of the Uwajima domain, and is also known for growing unshu mandarins. In season, mandarins ripen in the terraced fields around the area. Relax in the park and soak up the calm atmosphere of Yoshida, surrounded by sea and mountains.
quiz_en: Yoshida Park is in the Yoshida area of Uwajima City. Which local fruit is grown in the terraced fields there?

desc_en: Haraigawa Onsen is a hot spring in the mountains of the Tsushima area of Uwajima City. Tsushima lies in the southern part of the city and is blessed with both mountains and sea. Mountain streams flow nearby, and in this quiet setting surrounded by lush greenery, time passes slowly as you soak. Savor seafood from the Uwa Sea and the bounty of the mountains, and enjoy the relaxed air typical of the Nanyo region.
quiz_en: After soaking at Haraigawa Onsen, which local dish would you like to eat in the Uwajima area of southern Ehime?

desc_en: Namedoko Gorge straddles Uwajima City and Matsuno Town, and its name is said to come from the clear water that glides over a single slab of granite. Yukiwa Falls, deep in the gorge, is a famous waterfall where water flows down the rock face in a pattern like snow crystals. You can enjoy river play in summer and autumn leaves in autumn, experiencing the nature of the headwaters of the Shimanto River.
quiz_en: What is the name of the waterfall deep in Namedoko Gorge whose water flows down in a pattern resembling snow crystals?

desc_en: The Mishima Shrine Autumn Grand Festival is held at Mishima Shrine in the Honai area of Yawatahama City. Honai prospered through shipping and trade in the Meiji era, and streets that retain the look of that time still remain. On festival day, mikoshi (portable shrines) and other processions parade through town, filling it with local excitement. Amid the bustle unique to autumn festivals in southern Ehime, feel the traditions passed down in the town.
quiz_en: At autumn festivals in southern Ehime like the Mishima Shrine Autumn Grand Festival, which parade floats or processions would you like to see?

desc_en: Kurase Gorge lies in the mountains of the Kurase area of Tanbara in Saijo City. Surrounded by the rich forests of the Ishizuchi mountain range, its clear water weaves between the rocks. In the season of fresh greenery, vibrant green fills the gorge, and in autumn colorful trees decorate it. Saijo is a city of water known for 'uchinuki,' springs of underground water from Mount Ishizuchi, and here you can feel the mountain nature that is their source.
quiz_en: Kurase Gorge is in Saijo City. What are the artesian wells that bring up underground water from the Ishizuchi mountains called?

desc_en: Maegami-ji in Saijo is Temple No. 64 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage and is deeply tied to the worship of Mount Ishizuchi. It is the head temple of the Ishizuchi-san Shingon sect, with origins connected to En no Ozunu, said to have opened Mount Ishizuchi. The grounds are wrapped in greenery, with a solemn atmosphere fitting for the foot of Mount Ishizuchi. During the summer mountain opening, it bustles with many believers.
quiz_en: Maegami-ji Temple is deeply connected to a sacred mountain that is the highest peak in western Japan. What is the mountain called?

desc_en: Kichijo-ji in the Himi area of Saijo is Temple No. 63 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. It is known as the only one of the 88 temples whose principal image is Bishamonten. In the grounds is the 'Jojuseki' (wish-granting stone): if you walk to it from a distance with your eyes closed and pass your walking staff through its hole, your wish is said to come true, and many visitors try it.
quiz_en: Kichijo-ji is the only temple of the 88 with a particular Buddhist deity as its principal image. Which deity is it?

desc_en: Yokomine-ji in the Komatsu area of Saijo is Temple No. 60 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage, set high on the slopes of Mount Ishizuchi. The pilgrim path is known as a difficult section with steep mountain trails. Many rhododendrons are planted in the grounds, and in the flowering season the mountain temple is brightly decorated. On clear days, you can also see the majestic form of Mount Ishizuchi.
quiz_en: Which flowering shrub decorates the grounds of Yokomine-ji Temple, blooming from spring into early summer?

desc_en: Hoan-ji in the Kitagawa area of Komatsu in Saijo City is a temple with a history dating back to ancient times. Foundation stones of an ancient temple remain around its grounds and are designated a National Historic Site as the Hoan-ji Temple Ruins. Standing in a peaceful area of spreading farmland, it shows that Buddhist culture took root here long ago. In the quiet grounds, imagine the ancient temple buildings.
quiz_en: What are the stones called that remain around Hoan-ji Temple and once supported the pillars of ancient temple buildings?

desc_en: Dozenkei Onsen is a hot spring in the mountains of the Tanbara area of Saijo City. Nearby is a gorge called Dozenkei, where you can enjoy scenery created by clear streams and green mountains. Tanbara is an area where fruit growing thrives, and various fruits ripen with the seasons. After exploring the gorge, relaxing your body in the hot spring is recommended.
quiz_en: Dozenkei Onsen is in the Tanbara area of Saijo City. Which seasonal fruit would you like to taste after your soak?

desc_en: Toyo Onsen is a hot spring in the Shufu area of Saijo City. The Toyo region of Saijo is surrounded by plains facing the Seto Inland Sea and the mountains of the Ishizuchi range, and is blessed with abundant water. This easy-to-visit hot spring is a relaxing place for local people. After climbing Mount Ishizuchi or touring Saijo's springs, take a soak and slowly ease your fatigue.
quiz_en: After taking a break at Toyo Onsen, what local specialty would you like to taste in Saijo, the city of water?

name_en: Hijikawa Arashi (Morning Fog of the Hiji River)
desc_en: Hijikawa Arashi is a phenomenon in which fog formed in the Ozu Basin rushes down the Hiji River to Nagahama at the river mouth. It can be seen on chilly mornings from autumn to winter, and the sight of white fog blowing out to sea with strong winds is truly dramatic. The fog enveloping the Nagahama Ohashi Bridge at the river mouth is a spectacular view unique to this area and popular with photographers.
quiz_en: What is the name of the movable bridge at the river mouth, among the oldest still in use, that is wrapped in the Hijikawa Arashi fog?

desc_en: Mount Tomisu (Tomisuyama) in Ozu is a mountain known for its azaleas. Many azaleas are planted in the park near the summit, and in spring the slopes are dyed bright pink and red. From the top you can look down on the city of Ozu, the Hiji River and Ozu Castle, and it is loved as a viewpoint overlooking the castle town.
quiz_en: Mount Tomisu in Ozu City is famous for its spring azaleas. What colors would you most like to see covering its slopes?

desc_en: Shirataki Park, in the Shirataki area of Nagahama in Ozu City, is a gorge park with a series of large and small waterfalls. Its name, meaning 'white falls,' is said to come from the water flowing white down the rock face, and as you climb the trail one waterfall appears after another. The scenery changes with the seasons, from cherry blossoms in spring to autumn leaves, and in summer the coolness of the gorge is refreshing. It is a natural attraction near the mouth of the Hiji River.
quiz_en: For a waterfall walk at Shirataki Park, would you rather visit in cherry blossom season or autumn leaf season?

desc_en: Maruyama Park sits on high ground in the Yamatosaka area of Hijikawa in Ozu City. Hijikawa lies along the middle reaches of the Hiji River, a nature-rich area with villages scattered among the mountains. From the park you can view the surrounding mountain ranges and riverside scenery, and stroll while enjoying seasonal flowers and trees. It is a local relaxation spot where you can feel the quiet time of a mountain village.
quiz_en: Looking out over the mountains of Hijikawa from Maruyama Park, what seasonal scenery did you see?

desc_en: Ozu Shrine stands in the heart of the castle town of Ozu and has long been revered by townspeople as Ozu's chief guardian shrine. From its hilltop grounds you can look down on the streets of Ozu, and nearby are Ozu Castle and Ohanahan-dori Street, which retains its Meiji-era townscape. Stop to worship during a stroll through the castle town and reflect on its history.
quiz_en: After visiting Ozu Shrine, which castle or historic streets would you like to see in the castle town of Ozu?

desc_en: Okiura Kannon is a temple in the Okiura area of Ozu City dedicated to Kannon, the Buddhist deity of mercy. Located in a quiet mountain area of Ozu, it has long drawn the devotion of local people. The grounds are wrapped in greenery, and seasonal flowers welcome visitors. Ozu is a castle town along the Hiji River, and venturing out from the center you can discover countryside places of prayer like this one.
quiz_en: After visiting Okiura Kannon, what seasonal scenery would you like to enjoy in Ozu City?

desc_en: Koyabu Onsen is a single-inn hot spring deep in a mountain valley in the Hijikawa area of Ozu City. Its historic wooden building seems to blend into the green of the mountains, giving off a nostalgic charm as if time had stopped. Surrounded by quiet nature, you can soak while listening to the murmur of the river, forget everyday life and truly relax.
quiz_en: Koyabu Onsen is a single wooden inn in the mountains. If you stayed overnight there, how would you like to spend your time?

desc_en: The Hachimangu Annual Festival is an autumn festival held at the Hachiman Shrine in the Azo area of Ozu City. It is an important festival for the people of the castle town, with mikoshi (portable shrines) and other processions parading through the streets as the whole community celebrates. Ozu is a castle town embraced by the Hiji River, and in autumn, when cool breezes blow along the river after the cormorant fishing season ends, the festival's bustle signals the changing season.
quiz_en: Thinking of autumn festivals like the Hachimangu Annual Festival in Ozu, what kinds of events are held in your hometown?

desc_en: Otani Pond is an irrigation reservoir in the Kamimitani area of Iyo City. Iyo lies southwest of the Matsuyama Plain, where many irrigation ponds have been built for farming since long ago. Greenery spreads around the pond, and you can enjoy peaceful scenery with the surrounding mountains reflected on the still water. It is a relaxing spot loved by locals, perfect for a walk or a rest by the water.
quiz_en: After a walk along the shore of Otani Pond, what local specialty would you like to taste in Iyo City?

desc_en: The Suiha Highlands lie in the Hoo Mountains of Shikokuchuo City. They are known as a flower spot, with blankets of rapeseed blossoms in spring and swaying cosmos in autumn. From the highlands you can look down on the city and the Hiuchi Sea, where the factories of this papermaking town and the Seto Inland Sea combine to form a striking view. It is a popular spot for drives and picnics.
quiz_en: Which flower blankets the Suiha Highlands of Shikokuchuo City in bright yellow every spring, drawing many visitors?

desc_en: The Shiozuka Highlands straddle Shikokuchuo City and Tokushima Prefecture, with grasslands of Japanese pampas grass spreading across the gentle summit area. In autumn, the golden grass waves in the wind, creating a magnificent landscape. In spring, controlled burning is carried out to maintain the grassland, after which a carpet of green returns. From the observation deck you can view the mountains of Shikoku.
quiz_en: Which plant turns the gentle summit area of the Shiozuka Highlands a shimmering gold every autumn as it waves in the wind?

desc_en: Kawanoe Castle stands on a small hill in the Kawanoe area of Shikokuchuo City and is also known as Butsuden Castle. The current keep was rebuilt in the Showa era, and in spring cherry blossoms decorate the castle hill. It once stood at a strategic point near the borders of Shikoku's four provinces, Iyo, Sanuki, Awa and Tosa, and became the scene of fierce battles for control. From the keep you can view the town of Kawanoe and the Seto Inland Sea.
quiz_en: Kawanoe Castle in Shikokuchuo City is also known by another name. What is the castle's other name?

desc_en: Sankaku-ji in Shikokuchuo City is Temple No. 65 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage and the last temple in Iyo Province. Halfway up a mountain, it is reached by climbing steep slopes and stone steps. In the grounds is a pond said to originate from a triangular fire altar, and in spring the cherry blossoms are beautiful. From here pilgrims head to Sanuki, the 'dojo of nirvana,' as the completion of their journey draws near.
quiz_en: Sankaku-ji is the last pilgrimage temple in Iyo Province. What number does it hold among the Shikoku 88 temples?

desc_en: Enmei-ji is a temple in the Doi area of Shikokuchuo City. Doi faces the Hiuchi Sea and is backed by the Hoo Mountains, with peaceful farmland spreading out. The grounds are wrapped in a calm atmosphere and have been carefully protected by local people. Shikokuchuo is a city known for its paper industry, and places of prayer live on amid a life surrounded by mountains and sea.
quiz_en: Shikokuchuo City, home to Enmei-ji Temple, is one of Japan's leading production areas. What kind of products is it known for?

desc_en: Kannonsui is a natural spring in the Akema area of Uwa in Seiyo City. The clear water welling up from the mountains feels refreshingly cold when you dip your hands in it in summer. The surroundings form a relaxing spot with cool waterside greenery, and you can see people coming to collect the water. Uwa is a historic area where traditional streets and farmland remain.
quiz_en: If you touched the spring water at Kannonsui in Seiyo City on a hot summer day, how do you think it would feel?

desc_en: Katsuragawa Gorge lies in the mountains of the Nomura area of Seiyo City. Clear water tumbles between the rocks, creating a varied landscape of large and small waterfalls and pools. In summer the shade of the gorge is cool, and in autumn the surrounding trees change color to create beautiful scenery. Nomura is a mountain town where dairy farming thrives, and you can also taste dairy products made with its milk.
quiz_en: Katsuragawa Gorge is in the Nomura area of Seiyo City. What would you like to taste in this dairy farming town?

desc_en: Ryutaku-ji Ryokuchi Park is a park in the Uonashi area of Shirokawa in Seiyo City. Shirokawa is a mountain area through which tributaries of the Shimanto River flow, blessed with rich forests and clear streams. In the park you can enjoy strolling or resting surrounded by greenery. Shirokawa also has many geological highlights, letting you feel nature's blessings amid peaceful mountain village scenery.
quiz_en: Ryutaku-ji Ryokuchi Park is in the Shirokawa area of Seiyo City. What nature experiences would you like to enjoy in this mountain village?

desc_en: Meiseki-ji in the Uwa area of Seiyo City is Temple No. 43 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage and is affectionately known as 'Ageishi-san.' Its grounds, halfway up a mountain, are surrounded by trees and wrapped in a quiet, calm atmosphere. In Unomachi in Uwa at the foot of the mountain, white-walled streets and old school buildings remain, so you can enjoy a historical walk together with the temple.
quiz_en: By what affectionate nickname do local people call Meiseki-ji Temple in the Uwa area of Seiyo City?

desc_en: Yunosato Onsen is a hot spring in the Akema area of Uwa in Seiyo City. Uwa is a farming town spread across the Uwa Basin and is known for its rice. You can relax in the water while gazing at the peaceful countryside around you. White-walled streets and historic buildings also remain in Uwa, so you can enjoy a trip combining a town walk with the hot spring.
quiz_en: Yunosato Onsen is in the Uwa area of Seiyo City. What food would you like to taste in this rice-growing region?

desc_en: Karoto Onsen is a hot spring near the center of the Nomura area of Seiyo City. Nomura is a town in a mountain basin with a history of dairy farming and silkworm raising. The upper reaches of the Hiji River flow through the town, surrounded by calm, green mountains. Soak in waters also loved by locals and savor the unhurried pace of this mountain town.
quiz_en: After a bath at Karoto Onsen, what local flavors would you like to eat in the Nomura area?

desc_en: Shiroi Falls is a waterfall in the mountains of the Kawanouchi area of Toon City. Its water falling down the rock wall like white threads is beautiful, and it is also known for having been visited by Masaoka Shiki. The area around the falls is a lush green gorge, attracting people seeking coolness in summer and autumn leaves in autumn. In years of severe cold the falls can freeze, changing their appearance with the seasons.
quiz_en: Which haiku poet from Matsuyama is known for having visited Shiroi Falls in Toon City?

desc_en: Namegawa Gorge in the Myoga area of Toon City is, as its name suggests, a valley where clear water glides over a smooth riverbed of single-slab rock. In summer families can be seen playing in the shallows, and in autumn the surrounding trees turn red and yellow. Close to Matsuyama, it is loved by locals as a gorge where you can easily enjoy nature.
quiz_en: The name of Namegawa Gorge comes from the kind of rock that forms its riverbed. What is the riverbed like?

desc_en: Mount Sekizen is a mountain on Iwagi Island in Kamijima Town, known as a famous cherry blossom spot. In spring, many cherry trees bloom along the road to the summit, wrapping the entire mountain in soft pink. From the observation deck at the top, you can see the islands of the Seto Inland Sea and passing ships, a superb island panorama. It is a mountain of cherry trees carefully cultivated by the islanders.
quiz_en: Which flower turns the whole of Mount Sekizen on Iwagi Island in Kamijima Town pink every spring?

desc_en: The Niyodo River is a clear river that rises in the Ishizuchi mountains and flows from Ehime Prefecture to Kochi Prefecture. Its upper reaches on the Ehime side are called the Omogo River, and in Kumakogen beautiful gorges such as Omogokei spread out. The way its transparent water shines blue is called 'Niyodo Blue' and captivates many people. In the seasons of fresh greenery and autumn leaves, the beauty of water and greenery stands out.
quiz_en: What is the name given to the way the transparent water of the Niyodo River appears to shine blue?

desc_en: At 1,982 m, Mount Ishizuchi is the highest peak in western Japan and a sacred mountain counted among Japan's seven holy mountains. Near the summit are chain routes with huge chains, which ascetic practitioners and climbers use to scale the rock walls. The highest point, Tengudake, is a sheer rocky peak, and on clear days you can see the mountains of Shikoku and the Seto Inland Sea. Its autumn foliage is also superb.
