quiz_en: Mount Ishizuchi is the highest peak in western Japan and one of Japan's seven holy mountains. How tall is it in meters?

desc_en: Iwaya-ji in Kumakogen is Temple No. 45 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. Its main hall and Daishi Hall stand as if embraced by a towering giant rock wall, and some places are reached by ladders set against the cliff, conveying the austerity of a place for ascetic training. The deep mountain approach is wrapped in cedar groves, with an atmosphere full of silence and mystery.
quiz_en: The main hall of Iwaya-ji Temple stands as if embraced by a towering natural feature. What is that feature?

desc_en: Uchiko's historic townscape is a street lined with merchant houses that prospered from the production of mokuro (Japanese vegetable wax) from the late Edo to Meiji periods. In the Yokaichi-Gokoku district, beautiful buildings with white walls and namako-style tiled walls stand in a row, selected as an Important Preservation District for Groups of Traditional Buildings. Nearby is Uchiko-za, a playhouse built in the Taisho era, and traces of past prosperity remain throughout the town.
quiz_en: What specialty product, made from the berries of the wax tree, brought prosperity to the town of Uchiko?

desc_en: Ryuo Park sits on high ground in the Ikazaki area of Uchiko Town. Ikazaki is a town that grew up along the Oda River, known for its traditional washi (Japanese paper) making and for a kite battle held across the river on Boys' Day. From the park you can look out over the streets of Ikazaki and the surrounding mountains, and stroll while enjoying seasonal flowers. The peaceful mountain village scenery is soothing to the heart.
quiz_en: What traditional event is held on Boys' Day in the Ikazaki area of Uchiko Town, where Ryuo Park is located?

desc_en: Kamegaike Onsen is a hot spring in the Futami area of Ikata Town. Ikata lies on the Sadamisaki Peninsula, which stretches long and narrow toward the westernmost tip of Shikoku, sandwiched between two seas, the Uwa Sea and the Seto Inland Sea. Wind turbines line the peninsula's ridge, and open seaside views spread out. It is also a good stop on a drive to Sadamisaki Lighthouse at the tip of the peninsula.
quiz_en: Kamegaike Onsen is in Ikata Town. What is the name of the long, narrow peninsula stretching toward the westernmost tip of Shikoku?

desc_en: The Omoto Shrine Seimei Festival is a spring festival held in Kihoku Town. Kihoku is a mountain town in inland southern Ehime through which tributaries of the Shimanto River flow, surrounded by rich nature and farmland. With the arrival of spring, local people gather at the shrine to pray for the turning of the seasons and a bountiful harvest. In this traditional event handed down in the mountain village, you can feel the warmth of the community.
quiz_en: At spring festivals like the Omoto Shrine Seimei Festival, what springtime scenery would you like to enjoy in a mountain village?

desc_en: The Narukawa Gorge Cherry Blossom Festival is held in cherry blossom season at Narukawa Gorge in Kihoku Town. Cherry trees bloom along the clear stream flowing through the gorge, and the green of the mountains and the pale pink blossoms create beautiful scenery. Kihoku is a town blessed with rich forests and clear streams, and around the gorge you can spend relaxing time in nature. Enjoy hanami (cherry blossom viewing) while listening to the murmur of the river.
quiz_en: While viewing the cherry blossoms along the stream at the Narukawa Gorge Cherry Blossom Festival, what would you like in your picnic lunch box?

desc_en: Mount Sasayama rises on the border between Ainan Town and Sukumo City in Kochi Prefecture. It is known for the Akebono-tsutsuji azaleas whose pale pink flowers decorate the area near the summit in spring. Sasayama Shrine stands at the summit, and the mountain has long been revered as a sacred peak. On clear days you can see the Uwa Sea, the Pacific Ocean and the mountains of southwestern Shikoku.
quiz_en: Which flower, a member of the azalea family, colors the area near the summit of Mount Sasayama pale pink in spring?

desc_en: Ainan's Marine Park is part of Ashizuri-Uwakai National Park, and in the waters around Kashima Island a seascape of coral and colorful tropical fish spreads out. Warmed by the Kuroshio Current, the sea is highly transparent, and peering into it from a glass-bottom boat reveals a world like the undersea Dragon Palace of Japanese legend. In summer you can also enjoy swimming and snorkeling.
quiz_en: Thinking of the underwater scenery at Ainan Marine Park, which sea creature would you most like to see?

desc_en: Cape Komo is at the western tip of Ainan Town, where sheer cliffs line the coast facing the Uwa Sea. From the observation deck on the cape, you can enjoy a magnificent view of rugged reefs, blue sea and scattered islands. At dusk, the sun sinking into the sea dyes the surroundings red, offering dynamic scenery unique to the southwestern tip of Shikoku.
quiz_en: How did it feel to watch the sun sink beyond the cliffs at Cape Komo in Ainan Town?

desc_en: Kochi Castle was built by Yamauchi Kazutoyo, the first lord of the Tosa domain, and is a valuable castle whose keep, rebuilt in the Edo period, still survives. The main enclosure's palace also remains, and it is known as one of the few castles in Japan where all the buildings of the main enclosure survive as they were. The view capturing the keep from the Otemon Gate in a single photo is popular, and in spring the castle hill is covered in cherry blossoms.
quiz_en: Kochi Castle still retains all the buildings of its main enclosure. Who was the first lord of the Tosa domain who built it?

desc_en: In the Shikoku pilgrimage, Kochi Prefecture is called the 'dojo of ascetic training' and is known for the long distances between its temples. A culture of settai has been passed down, in which local people hand food and drink to henro (pilgrims) walking the long route along the Pacific coast. Precisely because the journey is so tough, the warm hospitality of the people of Tosa leaves a deep impression on travelers.
quiz_en: Kochi Prefecture, with its long distances between temples on the Shikoku pilgrimage, is called what kind of 'dojo'?

desc_en: Sawachi cuisine is a local dish essential to banquets in Kochi. Sashimi, seared bonito (katsuo no tataki), sushi, simmered dishes, fruit and more are boldly arranged on a large platter, and everyone helps themselves to what they like. In Kochi, where a banquet is called 'okyaku,' gathering around a big platter while sharing sake is the norm. It is a food culture that reflects the generous spirit of the people of Tosa.
quiz_en: In the local Tosa dialect, what is the word for a banquet like the ones where people gather around sawachi platters?

desc_en: Katsurahama is a beautiful bow-shaped beach in the Urado area of Kochi City, where the mighty waves of the Pacific roll in. On the heights stands a bronze statue of Sakamoto Ryoma gazing at the Pacific, making it a sacred spot for Ryoma fans. As the folk song Yosakoi-bushi sings, Katsurahama is famous for the moon, and its moonlit scenery is exceptional. Swimming is prohibited at the beach, so enjoy the views instead.
quiz_en: Whose bronze statue, a late Edo-period revolutionary, stands on the heights of Katsurahama gazing out at the Pacific Ocean?

desc_en: Chikurin-ji on Mount Godai in Kochi City is Temple No. 31 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage. A five-story pagoda towers over the grounds, and its garden, said to be the work of Muso Soseki, is designated a Place of Scenic Beauty. In autumn, colorful leaves decorate the grounds, wrapped in a solemn atmosphere. The Kochi Prefectural Makino Botanical Garden is right nearby, and you can enjoy it together with a walk on Mount Godai overlooking the city.
quiz_en: What is the name of the mountain overlooking Kochi City on which Chikurin-ji, Temple No. 31, stands?

desc_en: The Plum Festival is held in early spring, when the plum blossoms open, in the Higashigawa area of Tosayama in Kochi City. Tosayama is a mountain area in northern Kochi City with countryside scenery surrounded by clear streams and greenery. White and red plum blossoms covering the slopes announce the arrival of spring, and you can enjoy a walk through the village wrapped in their sweet scent. The area also produces citrus such as yuzu.
quiz_en: After feeling spring at the Tosayama Plum Festival, what local specialty would you like to taste in this mountain village?

area_en: Kochi City, Tosa City, Ino Town and Hidaka Village
desc_en: The Niyodo River is a clear river flowing from the Shikoku Mountains through central Kochi Prefecture into the Pacific, known for having some of the best water quality in Japan. The way its transparent water catches the light and shines blue is called 'Niyodo Blue.' Bridges designed to sink beneath the surface when the water rises are scattered along the river, and you can enjoy scenes of life alongside the river, such as river play and canoeing.
quiz_en: What are the bridges called that span rivers such as the Niyodo and are designed to sink beneath the water when it rises?

desc_en: Cape Muroto juts sharply into the Pacific Ocean, a place where you can feel the formation of the land of Muroto, certified as a UNESCO Global Geopark. Rugged reefs line the coast, and subtropical plants grow thickly. There is also Mikurodo, a cave where the young Kukai is said to have trained, and on the heights of the cape stands the white Muroto Misaki Lighthouse, shining over the vast Pacific.
quiz_en: At Cape Muroto, what is the name of the cave where the young Kukai is said to have undergone ascetic training?

desc_en: The Furusato Muroto Festival is a community festival held in the Murotomisaki area of Muroto City. Muroto is a port town where fishing for tuna, splendid alfonsino (kinmedai) and other fish thrives, surrounded by the magnificent nature of the Pacific coast. On festival day, local people gather to celebrate with dances and events, and the town overflows with the energy of a port town. Tasting the local seafood is another highlight.
quiz_en: Which famous fish landed at Muroto's ports would you like to taste at the Furusato Muroto Festival?

desc_en: The Aki Summer Evening Festival is a community festival held in summer in Aki City. Aki is a town in eastern Kochi Prefecture facing the Pacific, also known as the birthplace of Iwasaki Yataro, founder of Mitsubishi. On summer nights, local residents and people returning home for the holidays gather, and the festival bustles with events and stalls. Enjoy a Tosa summer night in the sea breeze.
quiz_en: Who is the person born in Aki City who is known as the founder of Mitsubishi?

desc_en: Kokubun-ji in the Kokubu area of Nankoku City is Temple No. 29 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage and the Tosa provincial temple built in the Nara period on the orders of Emperor Shomu. Its main hall, with a shingled roof, is designated an Important Cultural Property, and the mossy grounds are full of calm charm. The surrounding area was the site of Tosa's provincial capital, letting you feel ancient history.
quiz_en: The provincial Kokubun-ji temples across Japan were built on the orders of which Nara-period emperor?

desc_en: Zenjibu-ji in the Toichi area of Nankoku City is Temple No. 32 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage, affectionately known as 'Minedera.' It stands on a small hill, with unusual rocks scattered across its grounds and a sweeping view over Tosa Bay. Its principal image, the Eleven-Faced Kannon, has been worshipped by fishermen as a guardian of safety at sea and has also been called 'Funadama Kannon.'
quiz_en: Fishermen have long worshipped the principal Kannon image of Zenjibu-ji Temple. By what name have they called it?

desc_en: Nagaoka Onsen is a hot spring in the Shimosuematsu area of Nankoku City. Nankoku spreads across the eastern Kochi Plain, where rice farming and horticulture thrive thanks to the warm climate. Close to Kochi Ryoma Airport, it is easy to stop by at the start or end of a trip. At this hot spring among the fields, take a leisurely soak and soothe the fatigue of your journey through Tosa.
quiz_en: Nagaoka Onsen is in Nankoku City. What is the nickname of the airport that serves as the gateway to Kochi?

desc_en: The Usa Onabe (Big Pot) Festival is an event in the Usa area of Tosa City where a hot pot dish cooked in a huge pot is served. Usa is a fishing town facing Tosa Bay, blessed with fresh seafood. The flavor of seafood simmered in the big pot is exceptional, and locals and visitors gather around the pot together, feeling the warm hospitality of the port town. The seaside scenery is another pleasure.
quiz_en: If you gathered around the giant pot at the Usa Onabe Festival, what kinds of seafood would you want in it?

desc_en: The Usa Port Festival is a summer festival held at the port in the Usa area of Tosa City. Usa is a fishing port town facing Tosa Bay, a scenic place spanned by the Usa Ohashi Bridge leading to the Yokonami Peninsula. On festival day, people gather at the port to pray for safety at sea and good catches, and the festival bustles with events and stalls. Feel the summer energy of the port town in the sea breeze.
quiz_en: If you were to fully enjoy summer in a port town at the Usa Port Festival, what would you look forward to most?

desc_en: The Otsuna Festival is a summer festival held in the Takaoka area of Tosa City, highlighted by a tug-of-war with a huge rope. The sight of many people joining forces to pull the giant rope is powerful, and the venue is filled with excitement along with the cheers of spectators. Tosa City spreads along the lower reaches of the Niyodo River, and Takaoka, lined with shops, is the city's center.
quiz_en: If you took part in the giant tug-of-war at the Otsuna Festival, what strategy would you use to win?

desc_en: The Sotayama Yukiwari cherry trees are early-blooming cherries that flower in early spring in the Sotayama area of Susaki City. While the cold still lingers, pink blossoms color the mountain slopes, announcing the early arrival of spring. In some years they bloom together with rapeseed flowers, creating a vivid contrast of yellow and pink. Susaki is a port town facing Tosa Bay, where you can also enjoy local dishes such as nabeyaki ramen.
quiz_en: You travel to Susaki City to see the Sotayama Yukiwari cherry blossoms. Which local ramen dish would you like to try there?

desc_en: The Susaki Festival is a community festival held in Susaki City. Susaki is a port town facing Tosa Bay with a fine natural harbor, and it developed as a town of fishing and port industries. On festival day, local people gather and the town bustles with dances, parades and stalls. Enjoy the port town's energy while tasting the local specialty, nabeyaki ramen.
quiz_en: Amid the bustle of the Susaki Festival, what local food would you like to try in Susaki City?

desc_en: Enko-ji in the Hirata area of Sukumo City is Temple No. 39 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage and the last temple in Tosa Province. A legend tells of a red turtle that appeared from the undersea Dragon Palace carrying a temple bell on its back, and a statue of the red turtle bearing a bell stands in the grounds. In these quiet mountain grounds, pilgrims who have finished the demanding 'dojo of ascetic training' can finally breathe a sigh of relief.
quiz_en: According to the legend of Enko-ji Temple, what creature appeared from the undersea Dragon Palace carrying a temple bell on its back?

desc_en: Kanyojima Park is a seaside park on Oshima in Sukumo City. Kanyojima, the island floating offshore, is known as a famous sunset spot. On clear winter days, the sun setting on the horizon is reflected on the sea surface, and a 'Daruma sunset,' shaped like a daruma doll, may appear. You can spend a relaxing time gazing at the scenery of the calm Sukumo Bay and its islands.
quiz_en: What is the name of the winter phenomenon off Sukumo in which the sun setting on the horizon looks like a daruma doll?

desc_en: The Sukumo Citizens' Festival is a community festival held in Sukumo City. Sukumo lies at the southwestern tip of Kochi Prefecture, bordering Ehime Prefecture, and is blessed with the rich fishing grounds of Sukumo Bay. On festival day, local people gather to liven up the town with dances and events. Savor fresh seafood nurtured by the Kuroshio Current and experience the energy of the people of Sukumo.
quiz_en: If you joined the Sukumo Citizens' Festival, what seafood from Sukumo Bay would you like to eat?

desc_en: Cape Ashizuri is the southernmost point of Shikoku, where cliffs tens of meters high tower over the Pacific Ocean. At the tip of the cape stands the white Ashizuri Misaki Lighthouse, and the view over the endless blue sea is breathtaking. Nearby is Kongofuku-ji, Temple No. 38 of the Shikoku 88 Temple Pilgrimage, and a bronze statue of John Manjiro, a native of this area, also stands here. Camellias bloom in winter.
quiz_en: Who is the Tosashimizu native, honored by a statue at Cape Ashizuri, who reached America after being cast adrift at sea?

desc_en: The Ashizuri Citizens' Festival is a community festival held in Tosashimizu City. Tosashimizu, home to Cape Ashizuri, is the southernmost town in Shikoku and a port town where pole-and-line fishing, such as for Shimizu mackerel, thrives. On festival day, local people gather and the town bustles with dances and events. Experience the energy of the port town in an open, tropical atmosphere.
quiz_en: If you visited Tosashimizu for the Ashizuri Festival, which famous local fish would you like to taste?

desc_en: The Shimanto River is a great river that meanders slowly through western Kochi Prefecture and is called 'Japan's last clear stream.' Many chinkabashi, bridges without railings designed to sink beneath the water during floods, span the river, creating scenery of a way of life lived alongside it. You can enjoy river trips by roofed boat or canoe, and taste river delicacies such as river shrimp and wild eel.
quiz_en: Because of its beautiful, clear flowing water, the Shimanto River is often called 'Japan's last' what?

desc_en: The Shimanto Citizens' Festival is a community festival held in central Shimanto City, around places such as Tenjin Bridge in Nakamura. Nakamura is called the 'Little Kyoto of Tosa,' and its grid-patterned streets retain traces of this. On festival day, people gather in the town along the Shimanto River, and it bustles greatly with dances and events. Enjoy the summer energy of this town of clear streams.
quiz_en: Nakamura in Shimanto City, where the Shimanto Citizens' Festival is held, is called the 'Little' what 'of Tosa'?

desc_en: The Fuwa Hachimangu Grand Festival is an autumn festival held at the Hachimangu shrine in the Fuwa area of Shimanto City, known as the 'wedding of the gods.' Mikoshi (portable shrines) carrying goddesses gather from surrounding shrines, and unique rituals unfold, such as the mikoshi meeting one another on the Shimanto River. It is a traditional festival handed down from long ago, praying for good harvests and prosperity in the region.
quiz_en: Thanks to its unique rituals, the Fuwa Hachimangu Grand Festival is known by what affectionate nickname?

desc_en: Kochi Prefectural Noichi Zoological Park is a zoo on the hills of the Noichi area of Konan City. Its exhibits recreate the environments where the animals live, and with designs that minimize the feeling of cages, you can observe animals behaving much as they would in nature. The spacious grounds are green, and you can meet animals from around the world as you stroll. It is a popular spot for families.
quiz_en: If you visited Kochi Prefectural Noichi Zoological Park, which animal would you most like to meet and watch?

desc_en: Kuroshio Onsen is a hot spring in the Higashino area of Noichi in Konan City. Konan lies in the eastern Kochi Plain, a warm town facing Tosa Bay. Noichi Zoological Park and other attractions are nearby, so it is easy to drop by while sightseeing. True to its name, taken from the Kuroshio Current, you can soak and spend relaxing time in the bright atmosphere of southern Tosa.
quiz_en: After taking a break at Kuroshio Onsen, which spots would you like to stop by in Konan City?

desc_en: The Minakoi Port Festival is a summer festival held at the port in the Yoshikawa area of Konan City. Yoshikawa faces Tosa Bay, a fishing port town that has lived alongside the sea. On festival day, people gather at the port and it bustles with events and stalls. Feel the sea breeze and enjoy the seafood unique to a port town and the fun of a summer night.
quiz_en: Which seafood landed at Konan City's port would you like to taste at the Minakoi Port Festival?

desc_en: The Winter Summer Festival, held in the Akaoka area of Konan City, is an event where, as its name suggests, you can enjoy a summer festival mood in winter. Akaoka is known as the town where the folding-screen theater paintings of Ekin, a painter of the late Edo period, have been handed down, and old merchant streets remain. Lively events take place in the winter cold, and the people's energy warms the town. Enjoy this town festival born of a unique idea.
quiz_en: By what popular name is the late Edo-period painter known, whose theater paintings on folding screens are preserved in Akaoka?

desc_en: The Acacia Flower Festival is held in the Yasu area of Konan City in the season when the acacia blooms. In early summer, acacia trees bear white, cluster-shaped flowers that give off a sweet fragrance. Yasu is a seaside town facing Tosa Bay, with facilities for enjoying the sea and marine sports. Relax while feeling the scent of the flowers and the sea breeze.
quiz_en: Wrapped in the sweet scent of the Acacia Flower Festival, what would you like to do in the sea at Yasu?

desc_en: Ryugado is a limestone cave in Kami City designated both a Natural Monument and a Historic Site. Inside, stalactites and stalagmites create a mysterious landscape, and you can make your way through the cool air with a sense of exploration. A distinctive feature is the 'Kami no Tsubo' (Pot of the Gods), a Yayoi-period earthenware pot encased in limestone, letting you feel both natural and human history.
quiz_en: What is the name of the Yayoi-period earthenware pot encased in limestone that can be seen in Ryugado Cave?

desc_en: Befukyo Onsen is a hot spring in the Befu area of Monobe in Kami City. The nearby Befu Gorge is known as a famous autumn foliage spot, where the valley turns red and yellow in autumn. Monobe is a deeply mountainous area in eastern Kochi Prefecture, blessed with rich forests and clear streams. Soaking in the hot spring after enjoying the gorge's autumn colors lets you savor the tranquility and healing of a mountain village.
quiz_en: What is the name of the gorge near Befukyo Onsen that is known as a famous spot for autumn leaves?

desc_en: Hokigamine Forest Park is a forest park in the mountains of the Tosayamada area of Kami City. The spacious grounds have walking trails, an observation deck and a campground, where you can enjoy nature experiences in a rich forest. From the observation deck you can look out over the Kochi Plain, and on clear days you may even see distant mountains and the sea. It is the perfect place for forest bathing.
quiz_en: If you spent the day at Hokigamine Forest Park, would you rather enjoy camping or forest bathing?

desc_en: The Hamono Festival is held in the Tosayamada area of Kami City, known for traditional Tosa forged blades. These blades, such as sickles, hoes and kitchen knives, are traditional crafts made by forging and are prized for their sharpness and durability. At the festival, blades are sold and blacksmithing is demonstrated, letting you see the craftsmen's skills up close. Try finding a favorite blade of your own.
quiz_en: What is the traditional craft of forged blades, celebrated at the Hamono Festival in Tosayamada, called?

desc_en: The Tosayamada Festival is a local festival held in the Tosayamada area of Kami City. Tosayamada spreads across the northeastern Kochi Plain, surrounded by farmland blessed by the Monobe River and the mountains behind it. On festival day, local people gather and the town bustles with dances, events and stalls. Experience the energy of the community together with a visit to Ryugado Cave.
quiz_en: After walking around town at the Tosayamada Festival, what local specialty would you like to eat in Kami City?

desc_en: The Lake Okumonobe Festival is a lake festival held at Lake Okumonobe in the Monobe area of Kami City. Lake Okumonobe is a dam lake formed by damming the Monobe River, a quiet lake surrounded by deep mountains. On festival day, people gather on the lakeshore, and events unique to a mountain lake take place. Enjoy a summer day in the mountain village while gazing at the green mountains reflected on the water.
quiz_en: While gazing at the quiet mountain lake during the Lake Okumonobe Festival, what would you like to enjoy doing?

desc_en: Ikumi Beach is in Toyo Town at the eastern tip of Kochi Prefecture and is known as a famous surfing spot thanks to the good Pacific waves that roll in all year round. A white sandy beach stretches along the shore, bustling with swimmers in summer. Close to the border with Tokushima Prefecture, it offers open ocean views of southeastern Shikoku and is even called a sacred place for surfers.
quiz_en: What marine sport, enjoyed by riding the waves, is especially popular at Ikumi Beach in Toyo Town?

desc_en: The Nahari Port Festival is a summer festival held at the port of Nahari Town. Nahari is a town in eastern Kochi Prefecture facing Tosa Bay, a historic area where old merchant streets still remain. On festival day, people gather at the port, and the summer night bustles with events and stalls. Feel the sea breeze and experience the energy of this seaside town and the warmth of its people.
quiz_en: At summer festivals in port towns like the Nahari Port Festival, what do you look forward to the most?

desc_en: Kitagawa Village Onsen is a hot spring in the Kojima area of Kitagawa Village. Kitagawa is a mountain village spreading along the upper Nahari River, known for producing yuzu citrus. It is also the birthplace of Nakaoka Shintaro, a revolutionary of the late Edo period, and has a memorial museum. The Kitagawa Village 'Monet's Garden' Marmottan, a recreation of Monet's garden, is also popular. After enjoying nature and history, relax in the hot spring.
quiz_en: Who is the late Edo-period revolutionary from Kitagawa Village who was active alongside Sakamoto Ryoma?

desc_en: Umaji Onsen is a hot spring in Umaji Village. Umaji is a village deep in the mountains, known nationwide for producing yuzu citrus, and its yuzu drinks and other products are popular. A forest railway once ran here carrying Yanase cedar, and the village has a history of prospering from forestry. Soak by the clear Yasuda River and enjoy unhurried time in a mountain village wrapped in the scent of yuzu.
quiz_en: Umaji Village is known nationwide for producing a citrus fruit that is made into drinks and other products. Which fruit is it?

desc_en: Kizenzan Park is located where the Yoshino River makes a large bend in Motoyama Town. It is known as the place where Nonaka Kenzan, a chief retainer of the Tosa domain, built his mother's grave, and historic sites associated with Kenzan remain in the park. In spring, rhododendrons and cherry blossoms bloom, and the scenery woven by the clear Yoshino River and greenery is beautiful, making it a beloved relaxation spot for locals.
quiz_en: Who is the chief retainer of the Tosa domain who built his mother's grave at Kizenzan Park?

desc_en: The Ino Daikoku-sama Spring Grand Festival is a spring festival held at Sugimoto Shrine in Ino Town, affectionately called 'Daikoku-sama' by locals. Ino spreads along the Niyodo River and is known for producing traditional Tosa washi (Japanese paper). On festival day, many worshippers and street stalls fill the area around the shrine, making it a major local event celebrating the arrival of spring.
quiz_en: Ino Town, where the Ino Daikoku-sama Spring Grand Festival is held, is known for producing what kind of traditional paper?
